name: Haiku macro/sector rotation
strategy: Low-volatility, staples and utilities defensives, a gold hedge and a short semiconductor position, with 25% cash.
reassessment_note: The Round 3 book is up only 1.02 percent but has real exposure to the rate and rotation themes that drove the week. I want Round 3 to differ from Round 2, so I drop financials, energy, healthcare and the S&P 500 and rotate to non-overlapping defensives. USMV replaces SPLV for minimum-volatility exposure. XLU and XLP add rate-tolerant defensive sectors, though utilities are rate-sensitive, so I keep the weight modest. GLD is a hedge against the Treasury-yield and risk-off mix. A short SOXX position at 10 percent expresses the semiconductor breakdown, which accounted for many of the week's stop-outs. I hold 25 percent cash because the 10-year is near 5 percent and volatility is high. Gross overlap with Round 2 is zero: no shared symbols.

positions.thesis: Minimum-volatility US equities hold up in drawdowns and tilt toward low-beta, quality names. It is the book's core defensive at 25 percent with a tight 8 percent stop.
Utilities are a defensive with stable cash flows. They are rate-sensitive, so I keep the weight at 15 percent and do not go larger while the 10-year is near 5 percent.
Consumer staples are a non-cyclical defensive with low beta. They diversify away from the rate-sensitive utilities and the AI-led drawdown.
Gold is a hedge against real-yield stress and a flight to safety when equities fall. I size it at 10 percent with a 12 percent stop because it can whipsaw.

Semiconductors were the largest source of stop-losses this week (TSM, NVDA, ASML, AMAT, MU). I short the sector ETF at 10 percent to express the breakdown, with a 12 percent stop against a sharp reversal.
